newsitem.title: LIBYA: Sudan, Uganda hold reconciliation talks in Libya.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Uganda hold reconciliation talks in Libya.

text.p: Libya said on Monday that Ugandan and Sudanese ministers held reconciliation talks in its coastal city of Sirte to settle their dispute under a mediation by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.

Officials said that Ugandan Deputy Prime Minister Eriya Kategaya, who is also Foreign Affairs Minister, and other senior ministers met Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir on Sunday in Sirte, some 450 km (280 miles) east of Tripoli.
They also had separate reconciliation talks with Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha.

"There was an agreement on the basics (for a reconciliation) and there will be positive steps in the next few days toward solving this issue," Libyan Foreign Affairs Minister Omar al-Montasser who attended the talks said in a statement on Monday.
Uganda is facing a fresh wave of rebel attacks in the north. The dissidents have stepped up attacks since some 2,000 of their troops entered from Sudan last week.
"The agreement to be signed by our brothers in Sudan with various factions will be a base for a final solution to the issue...," Montasser added.
Gaddafi had a telephone conversation with Ugandan President Museveni on Saturday and also met twice with Bashir in Sirte.

Libya has been mediating between the two countries over the past two years in an attempt to solve their dispute and twice Uganda announced that Khartoum and Kampala reached agreements to normalise their relations.
